title: standardize-retry-after-idempotency-streaming-openai-compat
author: Maya Patel
description: This PR standardizes rate-limit semantics, idempotency key handling, and Retry-After behavior across the API surface (including streaming, tool/function calls, and the OpenAI compatibility layer). Motivation: we observed inconsistent Retry-After headers and error codes between streaming and non-streaming endpoints, leading to clients retrying incorrectly and creating incident INC-2026-02 (flaky client backoff). This change unifies the server-side behavior, improves operator observability for throttled requests, and hardens idempotency handling for long-running streamed responses. Changes include: 1) canonical Retry-After header semantics: numeric seconds for short backoffs (< 10m) and HTTP-date for longer backoffs; we now include a machine-readable "x-retry-after-ms" header for precise client scheduling. 2) consistent 429 payload format and error codes across REST and streaming SSE/WebSocket endpoints; the OpenAI-compat layer now returns the same JSON error body shape as the hosted API. 3) idempotency key lifecycle: persisted keys for streaming requests now record final status (completed/failed/aborted) and an expiration policy (default 24h) to prevent duplicate executions on reconnects. 4) streaming improvements: the stream termination protocol now sends a final control frame with canonical error metadata (code, message, retry_after_ms, idempotency_status) to make client retries deterministic. 5) compatibility shims for older SDKs: the TS and Python SDKs are backfilled to read the new headers and final control frames with a fallback path for legacy responses. The description below summarizes files touched, commits, review discussion, CI, and rollout notes.
